verdict: Chapter 5 contains no citations at all, so citation relevance cannot be faulted but an examiner will notice that the DID/VC mechanism, the limitation of role-based access control and the auditability role of the blockchain are asserted without support; three cautious additions from the existing list ([20], [11, 25], [2, 28]) would address this. The main readiness problems are internal contradictions produced by later overrides: Section 5.11 still describes temporal validity, revocation and lifecycle as future work although Section 5.3, Chapter 1 and Section 6.8 treat them as implemented, Section 5.1.1 states both eight and six Controller functions, the three-predicate 'current stage' decisions in Sections 5.2 and 5.5 conflict with the five-predicate current-stage decision in Sections 5.1.2 and 6.4, and several inserted paragraphs split sentences in half. The consent object C = (I, A, P, T, L, E) and the predicates VI, VA, VP, VT are consistent with Chapter 6, but VL appears under three notations and Av is defined once as participants and once as approvals; with the fixes above the chapter is submittable.
